context:
Goal: what you rule reaches its record, fast.
Problem (rule): owner rulings sent to triage mostly never reach main, and the inbox check passes as soon as a session names a home file that exists.
Based on (measured): 16 of the 563 notes in roadmap/outbox/triage.md carry an owner ruling with a time. 14 of those 16 have no match on main by slug search.
Based on (read): hooks/ruling_home.py checks only that the home path exists on some branch, not that the ruling is in it.
Departs from: main (decision owner-feedback-inbox: a ruling item needs only a home path that exists) — the item needs proof the ruling landed.
Meanwhile: the retrospective session (session_013NEJKz5AWFJhGvmCUoi6wQ) asks you in chat too and reads your answer; other work goes on.

options.gain: Rulings reach their record the same day, with no outbox hop.
options.how: Write at once. The session that hears a ruling opens a docs PR to the record in the same turn, and the inbox item cites that PR.
options.label: Write at once (Recommended)
options.lose: More small docs PRs in the batch queue, each with one review round.

options.how: Ledger plus check. Triage files rulings as today, but the item stays open until the record on main holds the ruling's time, and triage's status read lists the open ones.
options.label: Ledger plus check
options.lose: Rulings still wait in triage's queue.

short: How should a ruling prove it landed?
title: How should an owner ruling prove it reached its record?
why: It moves each ruling to its record in the turn it is heard, so no queue can lose it.
